summary: Klamath NF station staffed from 1914, cabin built 1925 on an enclosed timber tower; register says removed 1971 with only a foundation left.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan 4AR cabin on an enclosed timber tower
facts.status_note: Removed in 1971; the register says only a foundation remains

staffing.status: Named lookouts in newspaper items 1914-1941; manned only three weeks in 1941

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Klamath National Forest

events.note: Everson T. Rider appointed lookout on Dry Lake mountain (1914 newspaper item)
Inspection report: a standard lookout house should be built; the station is on Southern Pacific land leased by stockmen
Perry W. Fisher had spent 13 years as lookout at the Dry Lake station (1924 newspaper item)
Register: constructed in 1925, replacing a small shack used previously
Al Barnum succeeded E. L. Spencer as lookout operator
Forest Service road to the station completed for the Fourth of July
Klamath forest accepted title to 20 acres for the site, previously leased from the Southern Pacific Land Company
Register note: the lookout was only manned three weeks; R.C. Gibson reporting on August 8
Register and Forest Lookouts both give 1971; the register says only a foundation remains

corrections.why: The register describes a cabin on an enclosed timber tower; neither the register nor the Forest Lookouts page calls it two-story

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives a 6 foot enclosed timber tower with no total height; the brief's height_m 4.3 is not supported by either source, so the story gives no height and the editor should check it

sources.title: Dry Lake Mountain Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites register (Forest Fire Lookout Association)

notes_for_editor: Height conflict unresolved: brief height_m 4.3 (about 14 ft) against the register's 6 foot enclosed timber tower, which may be a height or a sizing figure; the story avoids giving a height. Current access is not documented in these sources; the 1960 Weebly entry ('Lookout opened by Nancy Hood. Could not get car all the way.') describes access at that time only and was not used in the story. The register credits its photos to the National Archives and the Nancy Hood Collection; no image URLs were found in the text, so no photo entries.
